saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even when the SAML operation failed; the failure is encoded in the SAML StatusCode and message.
saml.note: Do not flag HTTP 200 alone as successful SAML authentication.

saml.description: Token exchange may return a token with scope different from the supplied token; ZITADEL documents that scope can be extended or decreased.
saml.note: Scope changes during token exchange are not automatically a vulnerability; evaluate against policy and returned claims.

saml.description: When token exchange requests an ID token, the returned token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A.
saml.note: This looks odd but follows the documented RFC 8693 behavior in ZITADEL.

saml.description: Token introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience.
saml.note: An inactive introspection result may reflect introspector audience mismatch rather than an invalid token.

saml.description: Refresh tokens cannot be used as subject_token or actor_token in token exchange.
saml.note: Rejection here is expected and not an authorization-binding bug.

saml.description: User-facing identity fields commonly use ZITADEL login name such as preferred_username/username@primarydomain rather than the raw upstream SAML NameID.
saml.note: Do not treat the platform-formatted login name as an identity collision by itself.

saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even when the SAML response indicates an error; failure is conveyed in the SAML StatusCode/message rather than the HTTP status.
saml.note: Avoid treating HTTP 200 from /saml/v2/SSO as successful authentication.

saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow.
saml.note: IdP-initiated attempts failing are expected and should not be reported as broken flow handling.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST initiate the SP flow first and obtain a SAML request/intent before attempting SAML completion; IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid on this platform.

For SAML custom-login/programmatic flows, the fuzzer MUST bind the final SAML response to the exact SAML request ID and session token returned by the prior flow steps. Reusing a session token with a different SAML request ID tests the wrong thing and will be rejected by design.

ZITADEL documents that SAML errors on /saml/v2/SSO are returned with HTTP 200 and encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 alone as success for SAML protocol tests; inspect the SAML payload outcome instead.

For SAML brokered login with Login V2, user creation fails unless required fields are mapped from IdP attributes. The fuzzer MUST configure attribute-mapping Actions or equivalent setup before interpreting login failure as a SAML security rejection.

External IdP login is gated by login policy. The fuzzer MUST enable 'External Login allowed' on the instance or organization before testing SAML brokering; otherwise SAML login failures are expected setup failures, not invariant violations.

If organization-specific login settings override defaults, the fuzzer MUST include the reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} in the authorization request to exercise the intended org-specific SAML IdP configuration. Without it, default settings may be used and results will be misattributed.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. Requests outside that set are rejected by design and must not be reported as a bypass failure.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests, ZITADEL explicitly allows requested scope to differ from supplied token scope and says it can be used to extend or decrease scope. The fuzzer MUST judge the result against actual authorization policy and returned claims, not assume any scope increase is automatically a bug.

For I2 freshness tests on JWT-based client authentication and JWT profile grants, the iat claim MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. A failing request without these baseline-valid claims is an invalid test setup, not evidence of stricter freshness enforcement.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, the sequence MUST include a control token using valid temporal claims such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. Without a control, token rejection cannot be distinguished from bad client authentication or audience setup.

Token introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST introspect with a client that is in the token audience; otherwise active=false is by design and not evidence of revocation or freshness failure.
The token exchange resource parameter is currently not supported and supplying it results in invalid_target. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource for audience-binding tests on ZITADEL.

When requested_token_type is id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that returned access_token field as a bearer credential for subsequent API calls.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. Do NOT attempt IdP-initiated SAML login tests against ZITADEL as SP; start from /saml/v2/SSO or an OIDC authorization request that routes into the external SAML IdP flow. Treat IdP-initiated failures as by-design, not security findings.

For SAML broker tests that end in OIDC tokens, the fuzzer MUST include the OIDC follow-up steps: start_oidc_auth -> exchange_code_for_token -> verify_granted_identity. A successful upstream SAML authentication alone does not yield the bearer token used for verification APIs.

When testing SAML external IdP login on an organization with overridden login settings, the authorization request MUST include the reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may apply default instance settings and present a different IdP set, causing false negatives in SAML provider-selection tests.

External IdP login is gated by login policy. Before any SAML identity-brokering test, the target login policy MUST have External IDP Allowed enabled (default settings or organization-specific). Otherwise SAML login can fail due to policy, not due to assertion validation.

For Login V2 SAML identity-brokering tests that create new users, the upstream SAML assertion MUST provide enough attributes to populate required ZITADEL user fields, or an Actions V2 response manipulation on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent must map them. Missing required fields causes user creation failure that is unrelated to SAML security validation.

For I1 SAML signature-validation tests, remember that /saml/v2/SSO returns HTTP 200 even on SAML protocol errors; the actual failure is encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message. Do NOT treat HTTP 200 from the SSO endpoint as successful authentication.

For I5 token-exchange audience-binding tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. If the fuzzer requests a new audience not already present in either token, rejection is by design and not evidence of a bug.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests, scope may differ from the input request because ZITADEL validates and may reduce it. The oracle must compare granted scope in the response, not assume the requested scope was accepted verbatim.

For I5 token-exchange resource tests, the resource parameter is currently unsupported and always results in invalid_target. Do NOT use resource-based token-exchange failures as evidence of authorization binding issues.

For I2 freshness tests on private_key_jwt or JWT profile assertions sent to token/introspection endpoints, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Use template times such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for controls; otherwise failures may be due to malformed client authentication rather than freshness enforcement.

For I2 token introspection tests, active=true additionally requires that the introspecting client is part of the token audience. An inactive result from /oauth/v2/introspect can therefore mean audience mismatch of the introspecting client, not token expiry or revocation.

For I2 replay tests, do NOT flag replay of ordinary OAuth access tokens or JWT bearer grants as a vulnerability by itself. ZITADEL documentation describes opaque/JWT access tokens as bearer credentials and does not document jti replay tracking for general token use. Restrict replay findings to contexts with explicit one-time semantics, not generic bearer-token reuse.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. The fuzzer MUST initiate the brokered login through /oauth/v2/authorize or another SP-initiated entrypoint before sending any forged SAMLResponse. Direct IdP-initiated SAML testing against ZITADEL is invalid and will misclassify flow failures as security behavior.

For SAML broker tests, user creation on Login V2 requires required fields to be mapped from SAML attributes via an Action on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. Without this mapping, first-time SAML logins can fail because ZITADEL cannot create the user, which would be a setup failure rather than a security rejection.

When testing SAML signature and issuer validation defaults (I1), the fuzzer MUST distinguish ZITADEL acting as SAML IdP from ZITADEL acting as SAML broker/SP. The documented /saml/v2/SSO endpoint is ZITADEL's IdP SSO endpoint, while external SAML IdP brokering uses provider-specific ACS URLs shown in provider details and not documented as fixed public paths here. Do NOT assume /saml/v2/SSO is the ACS for inbound external SAML assertions.

For I2 freshness tests on OIDC tokens, include a control login using a valid token/code path. ZITADEL returns HTTP 401 for invalid or expired userinfo tokens and invalid_client for failed introspection auth; without a control, attack failures cannot be distinguished from broken client authentication or app setup.

Token exchange audience is restrictive by design: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. The fuzzer MUST provision subject/actor tokens with the target audience first; otherwise token exchange rejection is expected behavior, not an I5 violation.

Token exchange scope behavior is by design permissive in request syntax but validated by ZITADEL. When scope is omitted, it is inherited from subject_token or actor_token. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the exchanged token's actual returned scope/claims against the requested scope; do not treat mere acceptance of a broader requested scope as a bug unless the resulting token actually exceeds upstream authorization.

When requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use that returned access_token as a Bearer API credential; doing so will create false failures in verify steps.

ZITADEL currently rejects expired ID tokens even when used as subject_token in token exchange. For token-exchange freshness tests, an expired ID token rejection is expected and should not be interpreted as inconsistent behavior.
The resource parameter in token exchange is not supported and always results in invalid_target. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource to model audience tests on ZITADEL; use audience instead.

JWT private-key client authentication and JWT profile grants require iat not older than 1 hour, aud including ZITADEL's issuing domain, and a kid header identifying the key. Freshness or trust-anchor tests that violate these preconditions will fail before the intended security check.

Reserved organization scopes enforce membership and can change login routing/policy. For cross-org or multi-tenant SAML broker tests, the fuzzer MUST control whether urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or org-domain scopes are present, because these scopes intentionally constrain which organization and IdP configuration applies.

Introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. For verification, the fuzzer MUST introspect with a client/application that is in the token audience; otherwise active=false is expected and not evidence of revocation or freshness failure.
